questions.stem: A 54-year-old woman presented with a 4-day history of fever, myalgia, and headache. She worked on a farm near Savannah, Georgia. Though she did not recall any recent rashes or illness, she removed at least two ticks from her skin in the past month. She had a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes. She was taking losartan, metformin, and gliclazide. On examination, the patient appeared ill. Her temperature was 39.3°C (102.7°F); other vital signs were normal. Examination was otherwise unremarkable. Investigations: Total white cell count 2.3 ×109/L Platelet count 92 ×109/L ALT 84 U/L Peripheral blood smear:
questions.lead_in: What organism is most likely to be responsible?
questions.explanation: Ehrlichia chaffeensis HME, or ehrlichiosis, is caused by Ehrlichia chaffeensis, an intracellular pathogen that infects monocytes. The image shows morulae within monocytes. This is diagnostic for HME.

questions.question: A patient presents with fever, malaise, nausea, vomiting and leukopenia and is found to have this intracellular inclusion on microscopy. This inclusion is called a morula.
questions.question_raw: A patient presents with fever, malaise, nausea, vomiting and leukopenia and is found to have this intracellular inclusion on microscopy. This inclusion is called a morula (they provide you with this fact).

parts.text: What is the genus of two different organisms that cause this presentation?

parts_raw.text: What is the genus of TWO different organisms that cause this presentation?

questions.model_answer: (1) Ehrlichia (e.g., Ehrlichia chaffeensis, causing human monocytic ehrlichiosis; morulae seen within monocytes). (2) Anaplasma (Anaplasma phagocytophilum, causing human granulocytic anaplasmosis; morulae seen within neutrophils/granulocytes).

parts.text: Virus, parasite, and two bacteria transmitted by Ixodes scapularis.

parts_raw.text: Virus, parasite, and 2 bacteria transmitted by Ixodes scapularis

questions.model_answer: Virus: Powassan (deer tick) encephalitis virus. Parasite: Babesia microti. Two bacteria: Anaplasma phagocytophilum and Borrelia miyamotoi (also Borrelia burgdorferi itself, Borrelia mayonii, and Ehrlichia sp.).

cohort_answer.text: Virus: Powassan virus. Parasite: Babesiosis (Babesia microti). Bacteria: Borrelia miyamotoi, Anaplasmosis (Anaplasma phagocytophilum), Lyme disease (Borrelia burgdorferi), Ehrlichia chaffeensis.
